# 01 geo index -- 100 M point benchmark (plan 01 Z.3, Goal G4)

dbb9b19391 + this work), 1 FE + 1 BE in `apache/doris:build-env-ldb-toolchain-latest`, all caches off

## G4 verdict
G4 = "on >= 100 M points a city-sized polygon scans <= 5% of rows and wall time beats the bbox-prefilter
baseline by >= 3x".
- Rows scanned: city **3.33%** (PASS), thin 4.55%, concave 14.6% (its cover holds the 6.6 km-wide hole of the U).
- vs full `ST_Contains`: city **7.5x** (2,033 -> 270 ms), thin 6.5x, concave 2.6x.
- vs the planar bbox prefilter: city **1.0x (FAIL the 3x bar)**, thin 4.8x, concave 0.9x.  And the bbox is
  wrong: city bbox returns 2,727,994 rows, 763 fewer than ST_Contains (geodesic edges, see
  01.geo.es.mapping.md 3.3).  The index returns exactly 2,728,757.

## Why the index ties the bbox for compact polygons (profile, city)
| | index (geo_pts_100m_idx) | bbox (geo_pts_100m) |
|---|---|---|
| rows that reach ST_Contains | 3,333,875 (cover candidates) | 3,069,730 (in the box) |
| filter alone (no ST_Contains) | `s2_covers` 161 ms | `lon/lat BETWEEN` 150 ms |
| filter + ST_Contains | 257 ms | 259 ms |
| inverted index search (per tablet, 16 tablets) | 75-112 ms | -- |
| columns read | lon, lat, geo_cell | lon, lat |

For a compact convex polygon its bbox is almost as tight as a 64-cell S2 cover (3.07 M vs 3.33 M candidates),
and a vectorised DOUBLE range compare over 100 M rows (~150 ms on 32 cores, data in page cache) costs the
same as the BKD search + reading the candidates.  The exact ST_Contains on ~3 M candidates is ~100 ms in both.
So the 3x-vs-bbox bar is not reachable by pruning alone for a compact polygon at this size: the bbox is the
cheap lower bound of any scan.  The index wins where the bbox is loose (thin: 4.8x) and always against a
correct (geodesic) full scan (2.6-7.5x).

## Where the remaining time goes, and the next levers (not done in plan 01)
1. Exact recheck on candidates (~100 ms for 3.3 M rows): cells fully INSIDE the polygon need no recheck.
   An interior/boundary split of the cover (S2 `GetInteriorCovering`) would skip ST_Contains for most hits.
2. BKD search 75-112 ms per tablet for 64 ranges: data is clustered by id, not by cell.  A table sorted by
   geo_cell (DUPLICATE KEY(geo_cell, id) or a cluster key) makes every range a contiguous row span and the
   segment zone maps prune whole pages.
3. ST_Contains (S2 point-in-polygon) per row.  The bbox path pays it too.
